messages:
Ava (Design): Quick design review — small thread about the A/B variant chips + traffic slider confirmation. Thought: chips should show short label, percentage, and a subtle "active" border. How do we handle screen readers/keyboard and the danger state when moving >20%?
Riley (PM): TL;DR: need clear a11y labels and a confirmation for large reallocations (>20%). Also ask: should chip order be sticky or reorder by allocation?
Jamal (Eng): Sticky order makes backend mapping simpler. Reordering would require re-wiring IDs. Harder but doable. From infra: slider updates are live; we can debounce but large moves may cause transient canary spikes.
Sofia (A11y): Main concerns: 1) chips must have role="button" with aria-pressed when active. 2) each chip needs aria-label like "Variant Alpha, 12 percent, selected". 3) the slider must announce new value via an aria-live polite region. 4) confirmation modal should be keyboard-trap and use clear verb "Apply large traffic change" rather than just "Confirm".
Ava (Design): Nice. I sketched two options: (A) compact pill with percentage inside and a chevron to open variant details; (B) stacked list where percent is editable inline. I'll upload mock: https://redwood.design/figma/variant-chips
Riley (PM): Option B supports accessibility edits (keyboard + direct typing). But Option A is denser and better for dashboards with many variants. Need tradeoffs.
Jamal (Eng): Implementation note: inline editing needs an input focused on Enter; we can reuse the existing traffic-slider component. Will add an opt-in debounce and server-side validation to prevent instantaneous >30% jumps.
Sofia (A11y): For the slider: ensure step=1, min/max announced, and when a change exceeds 20% show a role="alert" region with message: "Large allocation changes may affect live traffic. Press Apply to proceed." That gives AT users the same cue as the visual red outline.
Ava (Design): Copy suggestions: button text => "Apply large change" and descriptive help text under slider: "Changes above 20% require confirmation to avoid service disruption." Also color palette: avoid pure red for critical; use #b02a37 for contrast but pair with icon and text.
Riley (PM): Agree. Also add undo window of 2 minutes with toast action "Revert allocation". Product wants metrics gating during rollout.
Jamal (Eng): Can implement temp fallback: when >20% change, we put route into pending state and show a progress indicator until backend confirms. If commit fails, auto-revert.
Sofia (A11y): Keyboard flow: users should be able to tab to chip, press Enter to open details, arrow keys to nudge slider by 1%, and Shift+arrow for 5%. Announce changes in aria-live when committed.
Ava (Design): I'll update mock and add focused states for chips and an accessible tooltip for the percentage. Will iterate on copy and add the confirmation modal design.
Riley (PM): Next actions: Ava to update Figma; Jamal to prototype debounce/validation; Sofia to test with NVDA/VoiceOver. We'll review in 48h. :thumbsup:
